title: US x Iran ceasefire by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if there is an official ceasefire agreement, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed halt in direct military engagement, between the United States and Iran by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET.

For the purposes of this market, an “official ceasefire agreement” requires clear public confirmation from both the United States government and the government of Iran that they have agreed to halt military hostilities against one another, or for an official ceasefire agreement to be otherwise confirmed to have been reached by an overwhelming consensus of media reporting.

If the agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to “Yes,” regardless of whether the ceasefire officially takes effect after the resolution date.

Any form of informal understanding, backchannel communication, de-escalation without an announced agreement, or unilateral pause in hostilities will not be considered an official ceasefire. Humanitarian pauses, limited operational pauses, or temporary tactical stand-downs will not count toward the resolution of this market.

A broader peace deal, normalization agreement, or political framework will qualify only if it includes a publicly announced and mutually agreed halt in military engagement between the United States and Iran, effective on a specified date, or otherwise confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting. Agreements that outline future negotiations or de-escalation measures without an explicit, dated commitment to stop fighting will not qualify.

This market’s resolution will be based on official statements from the United States government and the government of Iran. However, an overwhelming consensus of credible media reporting confirming that an official ceasefire agreement has been reached will suffice.

eventMetadata.context_description: The United States and Iran agreed to a fragile two-week ceasefire on April 7, 2026, brokered by Pakistan just ahead of President Trump's escalation deadline, pausing direct hostilities in the ongoing 2026 Iran war sparked by US and Israeli strikes in late February. This diplomatic breakthrough, blending a US 15-point proposal with Iran's 10-point plan, includes tentative commitments on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, though Iran maintains control amid persistent proxy attacks in Lebanon and Yemen. New Middle East strikes threaten collapse, while delegations prepare for substantive talks in Islamabad on April 11 to address nuclear issues, sanctions, and military withdrawals—key factors traders weigh for extension or breakdown risks.

title: The Masters - Winner
description:
This polymarket will resolve according to the player who wins the 2026 Masters Tournament.

If this player is eliminated from contention for The Masters based on the official rules of the tournament, the relevant market will resolve to "No".

In the event of a tie, this market will resolve according to the official winner as determined by The Masters official tournament rules.

If no winner is announced by December 31, 2026, this market will resolve to "Other".

The primary resolution sources will be the official results published by the PGA TOUR website and The Masters website. A consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Rory McIlroy's sizzling 5-under 67 in Round 1, capped by three straight back-nine birdies, propelled him into a share of the lead with Sam Burns, elevating trader consensus to a leading 24.5% implied probability ahead of Scottie Scheffler's steady 2-under effort three shots back at 18.5%. Xander Schauffele's solid start keeps him competitive at 8.4%, while Burns surges to 7.4% as co-leader, reflecting the deep field's volatility at Augusta National where course history, putting prowess, and green speeds often dictate swings. Scheffler's world No. 1 form and past major dominance maintain pressure, but McIlroy's pressure-free title defense as reigning champion underscores the tight race with no one separating decisively after 18 holes.

eventMetadata.context_description: California Governor Gavin Newsom holds a commanding lead in trader consensus at 27% implied probability for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination, propelled by a March 12 Politico poll showing him trouncing Kamala Harris in their home-state primary matchup and his high-profile book tour stops in early primary states like New Hampshire, enhancing his national fundraising and executive experience appeal. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez trails at 9% on her progressive base mobilization and youth, while Jon Ossoff's 6% reflects buzz from a viral February anti-Trump Senate speech positioning him as a battleground-state freshman senator. With a fragmented field and no incumbent, 2026 midterms, party endorsements, and Harris's post-2024 plans could consolidate support behind frontrunners amid uncertain primary dynamics.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket has HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. edging Vice President J.D. Vance (49% vs. 39.4%) as the 2028 Republican presidential nominee, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio third at 21.1%, diverging from recent national polls averaging Vance at 45% and Kennedy near 4%. This tight positioning stems from a massive April 4 trading surge on Kennedy—$3.5 million volume, boosting his odds 34 points—fueled by his Make America Healthy Again movement and family speculation, amid reports of President Trump's advisers weighing Vance against Rubio amid Iran tensions elevating the latter. Key dynamics include Trump's kingmaker endorsement, administration track records, and 2026 midterms; clear separation could emerge from explicit backing, primary straw polls, or scandals.

New York dominated their February head-to-head 111-89, fueling trader consensus amid Boston's depth issues and Jayson Tatum's return to the venue post-Achilles tear last playoffs. Recent Celtics momentum (four straight wins) faces testing against Knicks' three-game streak and seeding implications.

title: Iran x Israel/US conflict ends by...?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a continuous 14-day period without any qualifying military action between Iran, and Israel and the United States that begins at any time between market creation and the specified end date (ET). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

The 14-day period may begin at any time between the creation of this market and the specified end date (ET), and must continue uninterrupted through 12:00 PM ET on the 14th calendar day after the strike is confirmed. 

A "military action" is defined as any use of force by Iran, or Israel and the United States against the other’s soil, or official embassies or consulates, that is either officially acknowledged by the acting government or confirmed through a clear consensus of credible reporting. 

This includes, but is not limited to, airstrikes, naval attacks, and ground incursions. 

Cyberattacks, sanctions, and diplomatic actions do not count. 

Only actions by Iranian forces explicitly claimed by the Islamic Republic of Iran, or confirmed to have originated from Iranian territory will qualify as Iranian military actions. Attacks on Israel or the US by proxy forces (i.e. Hezbollah, Houthis, etc.) will not count.

eventMetadata.context_description: A fragile two-week ceasefire, brokered by Pakistan on April 7, has paused direct US and Israeli strikes on Iran in exchange for Tehran reopening the Strait of Hormuz, with negotiations set to begin April 11 in Islamabad. Strains emerged immediately, as Israel escalated airstrikes against Iranian-backed Hezbollah in Lebanon—deemed outside the truce by Washington and Jerusalem—killing over 250 and prompting Iran to restrict Hormuz shipping amid mines and wartime hazards. President Trump warned of "unprecedented force" if compliance falters, while mutual violation claims and low Hormuz traffic highlight de-escalation risks, with trader consensus reflecting uncertainty over extension beyond mid-April amid ongoing proxy clashes and diplomatic tests.
